subsystems.name: Regolith feedstock system
subsystems.role: excavates, screens and moves the raw material that is the building block.

subsystems.name: Deposition head
subsystems.role: places material in controlled layers — by extrusion or by direct melting.

subsystems.name: Motion platform
subsystems.role: positions the head accurately over the whole structure.
parts: gantry and rails, or robotic arm

subsystems.name: Printed shell
subsystems.role: the load-bearing structure itself — domes, vaults and arched walls that need no formwork.

subsystems.name: Radiation shield
subsystems.role: bulk material over and around the habitat to cut cosmic-ray dose.

subsystems.name: Pressure envelope and fit-out
subsystems.role: the printed shell is not airtight on its own, so a separate sealed liner holds the air.

subsystems.name: Power and autonomy
subsystems.role: runs the printer and the habitat without people present.
parts: solar array or fission surface power

buildSteps.title: Characterise the ground
buildSteps.detail: Map the site and analyse regolith grain size and chemistry — on Earth this is done with simulants such as JSC-1A, which mimic lunar soil.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Excavate and screen the regolith to remove coarse rock, then either leave it dry for melting or mix in a binder such as sulfur or a geopolymer.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the site
buildSteps.detail: Level a pad, build up berms, and bury or shield a landing zone so the structure is not damaged by dust and blast during later landings.

buildSteps.title: Print the shell
buildSteps.detail: A gantry or robotic arm lays material in layers of roughly a few millimetres to a couple of centimetres, following a path that builds arches and vaults without formwork — the approach called contour crafting.

buildSteps.title: Consolidate the material
buildSteps.detail: Layers are either cured if bound, or fused by microwaves, a laser or concentrated sunlight; in vacuum, sintering behaviour differs sharply from tests done in air.

buildSteps.title: Add shielding
buildSteps.detail: Printed cavity walls are backfilled, or loose regolith is piled over the dome to reduce radiation exposure for occupants.

buildSteps.title: Install the pressure envelope
buildSteps.detail: A gas-tight liner, airlock, life support and power are fitted inside — the printed shell protects, but the liner keeps the air in.

buildSteps.title: Commission and expand
buildSteps.detail: The habitat is leak-tested and pressurised, then further printed modules are added to grow the base.

prerequisites.tech: Robotic excavation and regolith handling in low gravity
prerequisites.why: digging is harder in one-sixth gravity and abrasive dust damages seals and bearings.

prerequisites.tech: Binders and sintering that work in vacuum
prerequisites.why: most demonstrations were done in air on Earth; vacuum, wide temperature swings and hard radiation change how material fuses and cracks.
no crew can supervise printing in real time, so the machine must detect and correct its own errors.
printing and sintering need sustained kilowatts through a two-week lunar night.

prerequisites.tech: Gas-tight habitable structures and life support
prerequisites.why: proven in orbit, but never integrated with a printed regolith shell.

pathway.milestone: full-scale Earth demonstrations printing with regolith simulants, driven by NASA's 3D-Printed Habitat Challenge (2015–2019)
pathway.unlocks: confidence that large layered structures can be printed from soil-like material.

pathway.milestone: robotic landers demonstrate digging, sintering and printing a small structure on the Moon
pathway.unlocks: real data on vacuum, dust and thermal behaviour.

pathway.milestone: an uncrewed full-scale printed shelter with overburden shielding survives a lunar night
pathway.unlocks: a proven design that crews can move into.

pathway.milestone: habitats printed by robots ahead of crew arrival, then the same method applied on Mars
pathway.unlocks: settlements whose structure mass is mined on site instead of launched.
